summary:
Moon on Earth: a data-driven search for lunar base analogs
We built a tool that finds places on Earth that resemble a permanent Moon base site. We first measured the Shackleton rim with NASA LRO laser altimeter data: mean slope 11° and slope spread 4.9°. We then screened Earth in 5 km cells using Copernicus elevation, MODIS temperature and vegetation, and JRC surface-water data. Vegetated ground and lakes are removed, and the remaining cells are scored and ranked by how closely they match the Moon target. The result is an interactive map, where the best matches cluster in the Pamir, Himalaya and Tibetan Plateau, with further candidates in Iceland and Patagonia.
This answers the challenge by replacing a short list of known analogs with a repeatable, measurable search. It is important because space agencies need affordable Earth sites to test rovers, cold-weather hardware and operations before flying them. Changing the target numbers lets the same tool serve other Moon or Mars sites.
details:
The project measures the Shackleton rim's terrain from NASA LRO data (mean slope 11°, spread 4.9°). It then screens Earth in 5 km cells using Copernicus elevation and MODIS temperature, removes vegetation and lakes, and ranks the closest matches on an interactive map.
Benefits: It is a repeatable, data-based search that shows why each site matches. It is reusable for other Moon or Mars targets and uses only free, open data.
Impact: Mission teams get ranked Earth test sites for rovers, cold-weather hardware and operations training, which lowers cost and risk.
Tools: NASA LRO LOLA, MODIS and ESA Copernicus DEM; EU JRC Global Surface Water. Python [confirm], Leaflet (HTML/JavaScript), VS Code, GitHub. Claude helped with planning and code.
Creativity: It starts from the Moon's measured terrain and searches outward, instead of starting from places people already know.
Factors considered: Earth can't match the Moon's gravity, vacuum or radiation, and temperature is matched only in relative terms. Antarctic Dry Valleys returned no valid cells, so polar sites aren't covered. Lakes and vegetation were filtered out to avoid false matches.
